title: ClearanceRule
description: One sourced minimum-gap requirement between two MEP system categories. A rule that cannot cite the clause it came from is not a rule -- see source.clause / source.text_hash below, which load_rules() in clearance_rules.py refuses to skip.

rule_id.description: Stable identifier for this rule. Carried onto every violation it produces so a reader can trace the finding back to this record.

system_a.description: One side of the pair this rule governs, e.g. 'electrical'. '*' matches any system.

system_b.description: The other side of the pair. '*' matches any system. Matching is unordered: a rule for (a, b) also matches a finding reported as (b, a).

min_gap_mm.description: Minimum required separation, in millimetres, measured centre-to-centre-free surface (matches Finding.distance_m * 1000 from geometry_engine).

axis.description: Which direction of separation this rule governs. 'any' applies regardless of orientation; 'vertical' and 'horizontal' apply only to separation measured along that axis.

source.description: The citation this rule was ingested from. All three fields are mandatory: a rule with no clause or no text_hash is refused at load, not silently dropped.

doc.description: Document the clause was read from, e.g. 'SBC-501' or a project specification section number.

clause.description: The specific clause/section within doc that states this requirement.

text_hash.description: A hash of the exact clause text at ingestion time, so a later diff of the source document can detect that this rule's citation has gone stale.

precedence.description: Where the rule comes from. 'code' is a statutory/code minimum. 'project_spec' is a project-specific requirement, which may only TIGHTEN a code minimum for the same pair, never loosen it -- see resolve_precedence() in clearance_rules.py.
